newsitem.title: DUBAI: Ramadan demand fails to lift Dubai gold market.
newsitem.headline: Ramadan demand fails to lift Dubai gold market.

text.p: Prices in the Dubai gold market have fallen in line with the weak global market despite improved demand in the first few days of the Islamic fasting month of Ramadan, traders said on Sunday.
"Demand is good at the moment. It is better than it has been in the last few weeks," a gold wholesaler told Reuters.
"With international factories closed for the New Year holiday, production has been a little less, while demand for the ten tola bars has been good," he added.

Traders quoted the benchmark ten tola bar at 4,960 dirhams ($1,351) in the Gulf trading hub of Dubai on Sunday, down from 4,998 dirhams a week earlier. A ten tola bar is 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold.

On the world market, gold was last traded on Saturday at $358.70/9.20 an ounce from $361.40/90 a week earlier. During the week it fell to fresh three-year lows below $355 an ounce before shortcovering and Japanese buying helped it recover slightly.

Traders in Dubai said the market was awaking from a slow year-end period, with sharply lower international prices, the Indian wedding season and more liberal rules on gold imports into India -- the world's biggest gold market -- bolstering the sales outlook.
"Normally, demand is good in the first few days of Ramadan, but slows towards the end of the month when people are preparing for Eid," a trader said.
"Good demand early on in the month is certainly the case so far this Ramadan," he added.
Moslems in most countries observed the start of Ramadan on Friday. The month is traditionally a time of abstinence by day and shorter working hours.
The end of Ramadan is marked by the religious feast of Eid al-Fitr which customarily involves the exchange of gifts -- gold being a popular present in the oil-rich Gulf.
